```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Rode et al. (2018) studied subcutaneous (SC) administration of turoctocog alfa
pegol (N8-GP), a glycoPEGylated extended-half-life recombinant factor VIII. The
paper fits two preclinical population PK models -- FVIII knockout mice and
cynomolgus monkeys, each fitted to simultaneous SC and intravenous (IV) data --
and then builds a human prediction model by combining the monkey SC absorption
parameters with human clearance and volume from the IV pathfinder 1 trial. The
three models are independent fits, so each is a separate model file:

* `Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_mouse` -- one compartment, Table S1.
* `Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_cyno` -- two compartments with dose and
  formulation covariates, Table S2.
* `Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_human` -- one compartment, Table S3 plus the
  Table S2 absorption parameters.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_human"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/jth.14013>
* Supplement (Data S1, Tables S1-S3): published with the article as
  `jth14013-sup-0001-Supinfo.docx`.

All three models are parameterised per kg of body weight, so doses are in IU/kg
and FVIII activity (FVIII:C) is in IU/mL; 1 IU/mL is 100% of normal.

# Population

* **Mice:** FVIII exon 16 knockout (B6.129S4-F8tm1Kaz/J), male and female,
  12-16 weeks. Three groups of 9 mice received 2500 IU/kg SC (flank, neck or
  lower abdomen) and 9 mice received 280 IU/kg IV; sparse sampling from 1 to
  72 h (Methods, "PK studies in F8-KO mice"; Data S1).
* **Cynomolgus monkeys:** six monkeys received 100 IU/kg SC once daily on days
  1-3 as either a 500 IU/mL (0.2 mL/kg, n = 3) or a 5000 IU/mL (0.02 mL/kg,
  n = 3) solution; five received a single IV dose of 100 IU/kg (n = 2) or
  250 IU/kg (n = 3). Sampling over 96 h with an N8-GP-specific
  (anti-PEG capture) chromogenic assay.
* **Humans:** clearance and volume come from pathfinder 1 (NCT01205724), in
  which 26 patients with severe haemophilia A received single IV doses of 25,
  50 or 75 IU/kg. Rode 2018 does not tabulate their demographics; Table S3
  reports parameters "for a 70-kg individual".

```{r population}
lapply(
  c("Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_mouse", "Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_cyno",
    "Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_human"),
  function(nm) readModelDb(nm)()$population$species
)
```

# Mouse model

```{r mouse-sim}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_mouse")
obs_mouse <- c(seq(0, 12, by = 1), seq(14, 72, by = 2))

make_single <- function(n, amt, cmt, treatment, id_offset, obs_times) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = treatment) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_mouse <- bind_rows(
  make_single(200, 2500, "depot", "SC 2500 IU/kg", 0L, obs_mouse),
  make_single(200, 280, "central", "IV 280 IU/kg", 200L, obs_mouse)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_mouse[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
sim_mouse <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, events = events_mouse,
                             keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Rode 2018: median and 95% prediction interval of FVIII:C after 2500 IU/kg SC (A) and 280 IU/kg IV (B) in F8-KO mice."}
vpc_summary <- function(sim, by = "treatment") {
  sim |>
    group_by(across(all_of(c(by, "time")))) |>
    summarise(
      Q025 = quantile(Cc, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q975 = quantile(Cc, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

vpc_summary(sim_mouse) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), fill = "grey70") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "FVIII:C (IU/mL)")
```

The published median SC profile peaks near 7 IU/mL around 18 h with the 95%
band reaching about 12 IU/mL, and the IV median starts near 7 IU/mL; both are
reproduced above.

The paper reports a SC Tmax of 14 h and a terminal half-life of 14 h. Both
follow from the typical parameters in closed form, so they are checked exactly:

```{r mouse-closed-form}
p_mouse <- with(as.list(rxode2::rxode(mod_mouse)$theta),
                c(ka = exp(lka), ke = exp(lkel)))
tmax_mouse <- log(p_mouse[["ka"]] / p_mouse[["ke"]]) /
  (p_mouse[["ka"]] - p_mouse[["ke"]])
thalf_mouse <- log(2) / p_mouse[["ke"]]
c(tmax_h = tmax_mouse, thalf_h = thalf_mouse)
stopifnot(
  abs(tmax_mouse - 14) < 1,
  abs(thalf_mouse - 14) < 0.5
)
```

# Cynomolgus monkey model

```{r cyno-sim}
mod_cyno <- readModelDb("Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_cyno")
obs_cyno <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 96, by = 1), 0.25, 0.5)))

make_cyno_sc <- function(n, form5000, treatment, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = c(0, 24, 48)) |>
    mutate(amt = 100, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_cyno) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = treatment, FORM_TUROCTOCOGPEGOL_SOLN5000 = form5000,
           DOSE_HIGH = 0L) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
make_cyno_iv <- function(n, amt, treatment, id_offset) {
  # DOSE_HIGH = 1 only for the 250 IU/kg IV dose (Table S2)
  dose_high <- as.integer(amt == 250)
  make_single(n, amt, "central", treatment, id_offset, obs_cyno[obs_cyno <= 72]) |>
    mutate(FORM_TUROCTOCOGPEGOL_SOLN5000 = 0L, DOSE_HIGH = dose_high)
}

events_cyno <- bind_rows(
  make_cyno_sc(200, 0L, "SC 500 IU/mL", 0L),
  make_cyno_sc(200, 1L, "SC 5000 IU/mL", 200L),
  make_cyno_iv(200, 100, "IV 100 IU/kg", 400L),
  make_cyno_iv(200, 250, "IV 250 IU/kg", 600L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_cyno[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
stopifnot(all(events_cyno$DOSE_HIGH[events_cyno$treatment == "IV 250 IU/kg"] == 1L))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
sim_cyno <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cyno, events = events_cyno,
                            keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Rode 2018: (A) 100 IU/kg SC on days 1-3, both formulations pooled 1:1 as in the study; (B) IV, dose-normalised to 100 IU/kg, both IV dose groups pooled as 2:3 (100:250 IU/kg) as in the study."}
sc_pooled <- sim_cyno |>
  filter(grepl("^SC", treatment)) |>
  mutate(panel = "A: SC 100 IU/kg x 3")
iv_pooled <- sim_cyno |>
  filter(grepl("^IV", treatment)) |>
  # 2 of 5 study animals at 100 IU/kg and 3 of 5 at 250 IU/kg
  filter((treatment == "IV 100 IU/kg" & id <= 400 + 80) |
           (treatment == "IV 250 IU/kg" & id <= 600 + 120)) |>
  mutate(Cc = ifelse(treatment == "IV 250 IU/kg", Cc * 100 / 250, Cc),
         panel = "B: IV, dose-normalised to 100 IU/kg")

bind_rows(sc_pooled, iv_pooled) |>
  vpc_summary(by = "panel") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), fill = "grey70") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "FVIII:C (IU/mL)")
```

The published SC median rises to about 0.2, 0.3 and 0.35 IU/mL after the
three doses, and the dose-normalised IV median starts near 2.8 IU/mL and falls
below 0.5 IU/mL by 24 h. The pooled IV median is dominated by the 250 IU/kg
animals, whose central volume is 49% smaller.

## Formulation effect

The 5000 IU/mL (0.02 mL/kg) solution has 32% lower bioavailability than the
500 IU/mL (0.2 mL/kg) solution; the paper's non-compartmental analysis found a
36% lower AUC. In a linear model the typical AUC ratio equals the F ratio:

```{r cyno-formulation}
cyno_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_cyno),
                            events = events_cyno |> filter(id %in% c(1, 201)),
                            keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
auc_typ <- cyno_typ |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(auc_0_96 = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))
auc_typ
auc_ratio <- auc_typ$auc_0_96[auc_typ$treatment == "SC 5000 IU/mL"] /
  auc_typ$auc_0_96[auc_typ$treatment == "SC 500 IU/mL"]
stopifnot(abs(auc_ratio - 0.68) < 0.005)
```

## NCA

PKNCA on the simulated cohorts: SC Tmax after the first dose (0-24 h) and IV
terminal half-life (0-72 h).

```{r cyno-pknca}
conc_cyno <- sim_cyno |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_cyno <- bind_rows(
  conc_cyno,
  conc_cyno |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(treatment, id, time)
dose_cyno <- events_cyno |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals_cyno <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, half.life = FALSE,
             treatment = c("SC 500 IU/mL", "SC 5000 IU/mL")),
  data.frame(start = 0, end = 72, cmax = TRUE, tmax = FALSE, half.life = TRUE,
             treatment = c("IV 100 IU/kg", "IV 250 IU/kg"))
)
nca_cyno <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_cyno, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_cyno, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals_cyno
))

published_cyno <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~tmax, ~half.life,
  "SC 500 IU/mL", 6.8, NA,
  "SC 5000 IU/mL", 6.8, NA,
  "IV 100 IU/kg", NA, 15,
  "IV 250 IU/kg", NA, 15
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_cyno,
  reference = published_cyno,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("tmax", "half.life"),
  units = c(tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  # keep only the rows the paper reports
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^[0-9]", Reference)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published cynomolgus NCA. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The Tmax of 6.8 h is reproduced. The simulated half-life is starred: the
two-compartment model built from the Table S2 estimates has a terminal
half-life of about 20 h (`log(2)` over the slow disposition rate constant,
computed below), which PKNCA recovers from the 0-72 h IV profiles, whereas the
paper prints 15 h. The printed value is closer to `log(2) * V / CL`, about
14 h, so it does not appear to be the terminal phase of the fitted model. The
parameters are kept as published.

```{r cyno-terminal}
th_cyno <- rxode2::rxode(mod_cyno)$theta
k10 <- exp(th_cyno[["lcl"]]) / exp(th_cyno[["lvc"]])
k12 <- exp(th_cyno[["lq"]]) / exp(th_cyno[["lvc"]])
k21 <- exp(th_cyno[["lq"]]) / exp(th_cyno[["lvp"]])
beta <- ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
c(terminal_thalf_h = log(2) / beta, ln2_V_over_CL_h = log(2) / k10)
```

# Human prediction model

Figure 3 of the paper compares 12.5 IU/kg SC once daily with 50 IU/kg IV every
fourth day over 9 days.

```{r human-sim}
mod_human <- readModelDb("Rode_2018_turoctocogAlfaPegol_human")
obs_human <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 216, by = 1), 191.99, 215.99)))

make_regimen <- function(n, amt, cmt, ii, ndose, treatment, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = ii * (seq_len(ndose) - 1)) |>
    mutate(amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_human) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = treatment) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_human <- bind_rows(
  make_regimen(200, 12.5, "depot", 24, 9, "SC 12.5 IU/kg q24h", 0L),
  make_regimen(200, 50, "central", 96, 3, "IV 50 IU/kg q4d", 200L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_human[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
sim_human <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, events = events_human,
                             keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Rode 2018: median and 95% prediction interval of FVIII:C for 12.5 IU/kg SC once daily (dashed, dark band) and 50 IU/kg IV every 4 days (solid, light band)."}
vpc_summary(sim_human) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50, linetype = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("SC 12.5 IU/kg q24h" = "grey30",
                               "IV 50 IU/kg q4d" = "grey75")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("SC 12.5 IU/kg q24h" = "dashed",
                                   "IV 50 IU/kg q4d" = "solid")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:9) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "FVIII:C (IU/mL)", fill = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

The typical steady-state average for the SC regimen is fixed by
`F * dose / (CL * tau)`, which the typical-value solve must reproduce:

```{r human-closed-form}
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod_human)$theta
cavg_closed <- exp(th[["lfdepot"]]) * 12.5 / (exp(th[["lcl"]]) * 24)
typ_human <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_human), events = events_human |> filter(id == 1),
  keep = "treatment"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time >= 192, time <= 216)
cavg_sim <- sum(diff(typ_human$time) *
                  (head(typ_human$Cc, -1) + tail(typ_human$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 24
c(closed_form = cavg_closed, simulated_day9 = cavg_sim)
stopifnot(abs(cavg_sim / cavg_closed - 1) < 0.02)
```

Day-9 trough and peak distributions for the SC regimen, against the paper's
statement that 12.5 IU/kg daily gives troughs of 2.5-10% and peaks of 5-15% in
95% of patients:

```{r human-trough-peak}
sc_day9 <- sim_human |>
  filter(treatment == "SC 12.5 IU/kg q24h", time > 192, time <= 216) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(trough = Cc[which.min(abs(time - 215.99))], peak = max(Cc))
tp <- rbind(
  trough = quantile(sc_day9$trough, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),
  peak = quantile(sc_day9$peak, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
)
knitr::kable(100 * tp, digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated day-9 SC FVIII:C (% of normal), 2.5th / 50th / 97.5th percentiles.")

iv_trough <- sim_human |>
  filter(treatment == "IV 50 IU/kg q4d", time == 191.99) |>
  pull(Cc)
quantile(iv_trough, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))

stopifnot(
  # Medians read from Figure 3 at days 8-9: SC trough about 5.5%, IV trough
  # about 3.5%. The bounds allow for digitising error and cohort noise.
  median(sc_day9$trough) > 0.04, median(sc_day9$trough) < 0.07,
  median(iv_trough) > 0.02, median(iv_trough) < 0.05
)
```

The simulated medians match Figure 3. The simulated 95% range of SC troughs is
wider than the 2.5-10% the paper states (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV percentages.** Tables S1-S3 give IIV as percentages. They are read as
  coefficients of variation of log-normal random effects, with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
* **Human CL-V covariance.** Table S3 lists "Cl-V covariance 24%" in the IIV
  column. The maintainers read it as a correlation coefficient of 0.24
  (covariance 0.0228). Reading it instead as a square-root-scale covariance
  (0.24^2 = 0.0576, a correlation of about 0.6) changes the 2.5th-97.5th
  percentiles of the simulated SC trough by less than 0.4 percentage points,
  so the choice is immaterial to every prediction shown here.
* **Width of the human prediction interval.** With the published IIV on CL
  (40%), V (25%), ka (39%) and F (14%), the simulated 95% range of steady-state
  SC troughs is roughly 1.5-15%, against the 2.5-10% stated in the abstract and
  Results; the paper's Figure 3 band is also narrower than the simulated one.
  IIV on CL alone already produces a wider range than 2.5-10%, so no reading of
  the IIV percentages consistent with Table S3 reproduces the published width.
  The medians agree, and the parameters are kept as published.
* **Human absorption parameters.** Following the paper, ka, F and their IIV
  are the cynomolgus values for the reference 500 IU/mL formulation. The
  formulation covariate is not carried into the human model.
* **Bioavailability random effect.** The scale of the IIV on F is not stated;
  a log-normal random effect is used. With 14% CV the individual F stays far
  below 1.
* **Covariate effect form.** "Relative effect" rows of Table S2 are encoded as
  multiplicative factors `(1 + effect * indicator)`, so the typical values for
  the indicator = 1 groups are 0.68 x F, 0.51 x V and 0.71 x CL.
* **Mouse injection sites.** The flank, neck and lower-abdomen SC groups were
  fitted together with no site covariate; the model has none.
* **Cynomolgus terminal half-life.** The printed 15 h does not equal the
  terminal half-life of the two-compartment model built from the Table S2
  estimates (about 20 h); it is closer to `log(2) * V / CL` (about 14 h). The
  parameters are kept as published and the difference is noted here.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on PubMed or the
  publisher site as of 2026-10-11.
